rationale: A wins because it does the ugly but necessary work of turning angles into reporting tests. Its line, "whether the message still means what it meant when a machine drafts it," is a real editor-facing tension, and the proof list drills into draft/suggest/send, defaults, recipient disclosure, and spokesperson risk. B's "The app that made women message first will now help write the message" is sharp too, but its proof asks are thinner; it sees the landmine, A tells you where the tripwire is buried.
gaps_in_A: "Dating apps are selling AI to users who say AI ruins dating" overclaims the supplied facts. One Bumble relaunch plus "some users" criticizing AI can become a conditional trend pitch, but the plural headline needs other dating-app examples before it leaves the room.

"the first substantive product move since the founder's return this year" is not in the update. The founder returned this year and the relaunch happened under her; "first substantive" is an invented sequence unless sourced.

"the company has made a claim the next disclosure will settle" is a little too neat. The facts say post-relaunch paying-user trend is not reported; they do not say Bumble made a measurable turnaround claim tied to the next disclosure.
gaps_in_B: "The relaunch is the founder's first big public move since returning as CEO this year" invents priority and chronology. The update gives a return and a relaunch, not that this was her first major public act.
"the user criticism of AI-assisted dating gives the tension a current voice" decorates a thin fact. "Some users have criticized" is sourceable only if you can show where, when, and how loud.

The first angle's proof list asks for "examples or screenshots," but misses the nastiest question: can the recipient tell an opener was AI-assisted? That is the backlash story if Bumble has no disclosure answer.

B leaves the conditional culture-trend route underdeveloped. It correctly refuses "Dating apps are all turning to AI," but it could have framed a narrower, provable authenticity-in-dating angle instead of stopping at three obvious doors.
